meanings: variant of 惡心|恶心[e3 xin1]

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 那个味道让我觉得很恶心。
example.pinyin: Nàge wèidào ràng wǒ juéde hěn ěxīn.
example.english: That smell makes me feel really nauseous.
example.fact: 恶 carries three unrelated-sounding readings depending on the word: è for "evil" (恶魔, "demon"), wù for "to hate, detest" (可恶, "hateful"), and ě only in this one word, 恶心, for "nauseous, disgusting" — a case where a character's pronunciation has to be learned word by word rather than predicted from a single rule.

examples.hanzi: 我吃了太多，觉得有点恶心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chīle tài duō, juéde yǒudiǎn ěxīn.
examples.english: I ate too much and feel a bit nauseous.

examples.hanzi: 这个人做事真恶心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge rén zuòshì zhēn ěxīn.
examples.english: The way this person behaves is disgusting.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中受伤了。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng shòushāng le.
example.english: He got injured during the competition.
example.fact: 受 (also seen standalone in 感受, also in this batch) works as a Chinese verb prefix meaning "to receive, undergo" — 受伤 is literally "to receive an injury," always framing its subject as the one something happens to, close in spirit to English's passive "to be injured" even without an explicit passive marker like 被.

examples.hanzi: 小心点，别受伤了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn diǎn, bié shòushāng le.
examples.english: Be careful, don't get hurt.

examples.hanzi: 他的腿受伤了，不能走路。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shòushāng le, bù néng zǒulù.
examples.english: His leg is injured and he can't walk.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 夜里很安静。
example.pinyin: Yè lǐ hěn ānjìng.
example.english: It's very quiet at night.
example.fact: 夜 is night as a span of time; in everyday speech people more often say 晚上 (evening/night). 夜 appears in 夜里 (at night), 夜市 (night market, a beloved institution), 夜宵 (late-night snack) and 熬夜 (to stay up late).

examples.hanzi: 他夜里常常睡不着。
examples.pinyin: Tā yè lǐ chángcháng shuì bu zháo.
examples.english: He often can't sleep at night.

examples.hanzi: 今天晚上是个月圆之夜。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang shì gè yuè yuán zhī yè.
examples.english: Tonight is a full moon night.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a family of female words: 妈, 姐, 妹; 婊 is a vulgar term.
表 (biǎo) sounds exactly like 婊.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那部电视剧里,有人骂女主角是“婊子”。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànshìjù lǐ, yǒurén mà nǚzhǔjué shì “biǎozi”.
example.english: In that TV drama, someone calls the female lead a "whore."
example.fact: 婊子 is a strongly vulgar, offensive insult in Mandarin, roughly on par with its English gloss — it turns up often in fiction, drama dialogue, and online arguments to paint a character as crude, but it is not a word to reach for casually in real conversation; the character 婊 itself rarely appears outside this word and its close slang derivatives.

examples.hanzi: 老师说不要用“婊子”这样的脏话。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō búyào yòng “biǎozi” zhèyàng de zānghuà.
examples.english: The teacher said not to use foul language like "biǎozi".

examples.hanzi: 这个词是脏话，我们不要说婊子这个词。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cí shì zānghuà, wǒmen búyào shuō biǎozi zhè ge cí.
examples.english: This word is vulgar, so we shouldn't say the word biǎozi.

components.note: 尸 (body, building) — dwelling and body words: 居, 屋, 层; 属 is to belong to a family or group.
Traditional 屬 had 蜀 (shǔ) as sound part, also in 独 dú, 烛 zhú, 触 chù; simplified 属 keeps the reading shǔ.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 这本书属于图书馆。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shǔyú túshūguǎn.
example.english: This book belongs to the library.
example.fact: 属于 always takes the owner or category directly as its object (X属于Y, "X belongs to Y") — unlike English "belong," which needs the extra word "to," Chinese 属于 is never split into a separate verb plus preposition; 于 already fuses that "to" meaning onto 属.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车属于我哥哥。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē shǔyú wǒ gēge.
examples.english: This car belongs to my older brother.

examples.hanzi: 鲸鱼属于哺乳动物。
examples.pinyin: Jīngyú shǔyú bǔrǔ dòngwù.
examples.english: Whales are mammals.

components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and stepping: 跑, 跳, 踢; 蹈 is to tread or stamp.
舀 (yǎo) is a loose clue; same part in 稻 dào and 滔 tāo.

example.hanzi: 她从小就学习舞蹈。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xuéxí wǔdǎo.
example.english: She has studied dance since childhood.
example.fact: 舞蹈 doubles two characters that each independently mean "to dance": 舞 (pictured with a dancer's sleeves above and a pair of feet 舛 below) and 蹈 (足 "foot" plus a phonetic) — the same synonym-doubling strategy behind 拒绝 and 邀请 elsewhere in this batch.

examples.hanzi: 她在舞蹈比赛中得了奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǔdǎo bǐsài zhōng déle jiǎng.
examples.english: She won a prize in the dance competition.

examples.hanzi: 我想报名学习民族舞蹈。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bàomíng xuéxí mínzú wǔdǎo.
examples.english: I'd like to sign up to learn folk dance.

components.note: 木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 本: 根 is a root.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for gēn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn and 很 hěn.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to grip or rely on.
居 (jū) is a close sound clue for jù; 居 also in 剧 jù and 锯 jù.

example.hanzi: 根据报告,今年的销售额有所增长。
example.pinyin: Gēnjù bàogào, jīnnián de xiāoshòu'é yǒusuǒ zēngzhǎng.
example.english: According to the report, this year's sales have increased somewhat.
example.fact: 根据 does double grammatical duty: a preposition ("according to," placed before a noun phrase, as here) and a countable noun ("a basis, grounds," as in 有根据 "well-founded," fittingly the classifier 个 is listed right in its own dictionary entry) — one more Chinese word that switches role for free where English often needs two different words.

examples.hanzi: 根据天气预报，明天会下雨。
examples.pinyin: Gēnjù tiānqì yùbào, míngtiān huì xià yǔ.
examples.english: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这个结论没有根据。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiélùn méiyǒu gēnjù.
examples.english: This conclusion has no basis.

components.note: 几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.
乎 (hū) — as a sound part it gives hū to 呼 (call out, breathe out), so 呼 and 乎 sound the same.

example.hanzi: 他几乎每天都跑步。
example.pinyin: Tā jīhū měitiān dōu pǎobù.
example.english: He runs almost every day.
example.fact: 几 changes its reading depending on the word: jǐ means "how many, a few" (几个人, "how many/some people"), but in 几乎 and a small set of other words (茶几, "a small table") it is read jī instead — another case, like 恶心, where a character's reading has to be learned per word rather than derived from one rule.

examples.hanzi: 我几乎忘了今天是你的生日。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīhū wàngle jīntiān shì nǐ de shēngrì.
examples.english: I almost forgot that today is your birthday.

examples.hanzi: 他几乎没吃什么东西。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīhū méi chī shénme dōngxi.
examples.english: He hardly ate anything.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这道菜算是我们店里的招牌菜。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài suànshì wǒmen diàn lǐ de zhāopáicài.
example.english: This dish counts as our restaurant's signature dish.
example.fact: 算 already covers both "to calculate" and, more loosely, "to count as, to qualify as" — 算是 simply locks in that second, looser sense with 是 ("to be"), turning an arithmetic verb into a hedge for tentative or approximate classification ("counts as," "is more or less").

examples.hanzi: 他算是我的老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā suànshì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: He counts as my teacher.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试，我算是及格了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì, wǒ suànshì jígé le.
examples.english: On this exam, I more or less passed.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.

example.hanzi: 他在这部电影里演医生。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǎn yīshēng.
example.english: He plays a doctor in this film.
example.fact: 演 takes the role directly as its object: 演医生 means "play a doctor". It is the root of 表演 (perform), 演员 (actor), 演出 (a show), 演讲 (speech) and 演唱会 (concert).

examples.hanzi: 她演得很好，大家都喜欢她。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǎn de hěn hǎo, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: She acts very well and everyone likes her.

examples.hanzi: 学生们在台上演节目。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài tái shang yǎn jiémù.
examples.english: The students are putting on a show on stage.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 这个问题的答案很简单。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí de dá'àn hěn jiǎndān.
example.english: The answer to this question is very simple.
example.fact: 答案 pairs the verb root 答 ("to answer, reply") with 案 ("a case, file, record"), giving the image of an answer as something formally set down — not unlike how English "case" and "file" both extend from physical documents to abstract records.

examples.hanzi: 你的答案对了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de dá'àn duì le ma?
examples.english: Is your answer right?

examples.hanzi: 我还在找这道题的答案。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái zài zhǎo zhè dào tí de dá'àn.
examples.english: I'm still looking for the answer to this question.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 他在这次比赛中表现得非常出色。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhè cì bǐsài zhōng biǎoxiàn de fēicháng chūsè.
example.english: He performed extremely well in this competition.
example.fact: 出色 literally means "to step outside of [ordinary] color/hue" (出 "to emerge, exceed" plus 色 "color, appearance") — much like English "outstanding" (literally "standing out"), two unrelated languages independently reached for a spatial image of exceeding the ordinary to describe excellence.

examples.hanzi: 她的中文说得很出色。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén shuō de hěn chūsè.
examples.english: She speaks Chinese very well.

examples.hanzi: 这位出色的厨师做了一桌好菜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi chūsè de chúshī zuòle yì zhuō hǎo cài.
examples.english: This outstanding chef cooked a table of great dishes.

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 目前情况还不太清楚。
example.pinyin: Mùqián qíngkuàng hái bú tài qīngchǔ.
example.english: The situation is still not very clear at present.
example.fact: 目前 literally means "before the eye(s)" (目 "eye" + 前 "in front of") — the same spatial metaphor for the present moment recurs in 眼前 ("right before one's eyes," also meaning "right now"), built from a different "eye" character on the same logic.

examples.hanzi: 我目前住在朋友家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mùqián zhù zài péngyou jiā.
examples.english: I'm currently staying at a friend's place.

examples.hanzi: 目前还没有结果。
examples.pinyin: Mùqián hái méiyǒu jiéguǒ.
examples.english: There are no results yet.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 医生让我每天多活动活动。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng wǒ měitiān duō huódòng huódòng.
example.english: The doctor told me to move around more every day.
example.fact: Reduplicating 活动 into 活动活动 softens it into a casual, low-commitment suggestion — "just move around a bit" — the same reduplication pattern seen in 谢谢 and 试试, where repeating a verb makes the action sound lighter and less demanding.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去参加活动吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù cānjiā huódòng ba.
examples.english: Let's go to an event this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 学校举办了很多课外活动。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào jǔbànle hěn duō kèwài huódòng.
examples.english: The school held many extracurricular activities.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 成为一名医生是她的梦想。
example.pinyin: Chéngwéi yì míng yīshēng shì tā de mèngxiǎng.
example.english: Becoming a doctor is her dream.
example.fact: 梦想 (an aspiration, "dream" in the sense of a life goal) is a different word from 梦 alone or 做梦 (the literal dream one has while asleep) — English collapses both senses into a single word "dream," but Chinese keeps the sleep-dream and the aspiration mostly apart in everyday use.

examples.hanzi: 我的梦想是环游世界。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de mèngxiǎng shì huányóu shìjiè.
examples.english: My dream is to travel around the world.

examples.hanzi: 你要坚持自己的梦想。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào jiānchí zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: You should hold on to your dream.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁, 钱, 银; 锁 is a metal lock. The right side matches 琐 suǒ and 唢 suǒ.

example.hanzi: 请把门锁好。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén suǒ hǎo.
example.english: Please lock the door.
example.fact: 锁 is both the noun (一把锁, with the measure word 把) and the verb (锁门, 锁上). It is handy in modern vocabulary too: 锁屏 means to lock a phone screen, and 封锁 means to blockade.

examples.hanzi: 我找不到锁的钥匙了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào suǒ de yàoshi le.
examples.english: I can't find the key to the lock.

examples.hanzi: 出门时别忘了锁门。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén shí bié wàng le suǒ mén.
examples.english: Don't forget to lock the door when you go out.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.

example.hanzi: 经过多次尝试,他最终成功了。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò duō cì chángshì, tā zuìzhōng chénggōng le.
example.english: After many attempts, he finally succeeded.
example.fact: 最 (built from 日 "sun" plus 取 "to take, gather" — everything gathered under the sun, i.e. "the utmost") is Chinese's core superlative marker, forming the "-est" of almost any adjective (最好 "best," 最大 "biggest") — 最终 simply applies that same superlative logic to 终 ("the end"), giving "the very last, final."

examples.hanzi: 最终的结果让大家很满意。
examples.pinyin: Zuìzhōng de jiéguǒ ràng dàjiā hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: The final result made everyone very satisfied.

examples.hanzi: 最终，我们赢得了比赛。
examples.pinyin: Zuìzhōng, wǒmen yíngdéle bǐsài.
examples.english: In the end, we won the match.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这个游乐场只适合大人,不适合小孩。
example.pinyin: Zhège yóulèchǎng zhǐ shìhé dàren, bú shìhé xiǎohái.
example.english: This amusement park is only suitable for adults, not children.
example.fact: As "adult, grownup" this word is read with a neutral tone, dàren; but in period dramas and formal historical address (roughly "your honor"), the same two characters are instead read dàrén, with a full second tone on 人 — a reading split not unlike how 东西 (also flagged in the pilot batch) shifts meaning between its toned and neutral-toned forms.

examples.hanzi: 大人们在客厅聊天。
examples.pinyin: Dàrenmen zài kètīng liáotiān.
examples.english: The adults are chatting in the living room.

examples.hanzi: 等你长大了，就是大人了。
examples.pinyin: Děng nǐ zhǎng dà le, jiù shì dàren le.
examples.english: When you grow up, you'll be an adult.

components.note: 冉 (rǎn) — the main part. The dictionary story is two fish on a line 一: a second catch, so 'again'. It is a memory aid; the origin is unclear.
一 (one) — the top bar. Memory aid: 'one more' line on top — 再见 see you again, 再次 once more.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.hanzi: 请再次确认您的信息。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zàicì quèrèn nín de xìnxī.
example.english: Please confirm your information once more.
example.fact: 再次 is a more formal, written-register synonym for the everyday adverb 再 ("again") — 请再次确认 ("please confirm again") reads like an instruction manual or official notice, whereas casual speech would simply say 再确认一下.

examples.hanzi: 请你再次检查一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zàicì jiǎnchá yíxià.
examples.english: Please check it once more.

examples.hanzi: 我们明年再次见面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngnián zàicì jiànmiàn.
examples.english: We'll meet again next year.

components.note: 旡 (turned-away person) — someone turning from the food 皀 after eating: already done. Compare 即, who is just about to eat.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 既然你已经决定了,我就不再劝你了。
example.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, wǒ jiù bú zài quàn nǐ le.
example.english: Since you've already decided, I won't try to persuade you anymore.
example.fact: 既然 almost always sets up a matching 就 later in the sentence ("既然...,就...") to draw a conclusion from an accepted premise — a paired-clause structure much like "因为...,所以..." (also flagged in the pilot batch), where the first half states a given fact and the second draws what naturally follows.

examples.hanzi: 既然你不舒服，就回家休息吧。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ bù shūfu, jiù huí jiā xiūxi ba.
examples.english: Since you feel unwell, go home and rest.

examples.hanzi: 既然来了，就多玩几天吧。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán lái le, jiù duō wán jǐ tiān ba.
examples.english: Since you're here, stay and have fun for a few more days.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 请所有工作人员到会议室集合。
example.pinyin: Qǐng suǒyǒu gōngzuò rényuán dào huìyìshì jíhé.
example.english: Please have all staff members gather in the meeting room.
example.fact: 人员 rarely stands completely alone — it usually attaches to a role or department to specify which staff is meant, as in 工作人员 ("work personnel, staff") here or 医护人员 ("medical personnel"); bare 人员 by itself reads as oddly abstract, almost bureaucratic, in casual speech.

examples.hanzi: 酒店的工作人员很热情。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn de gōngzuò rényuán hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: The hotel staff are very friendly.

examples.hanzi: 公司新来了几名技术人员。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xīn láile jǐ míng jìshù rényuán.
examples.english: A few new technical staff joined the company.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 集, 难, 雀; 雄 male and 雌 female were first words for birds of each sex.
厷 (gōng) is a loose sound clue for xióng.

example.hanzi: 他是很多孩子心中的英雄。
example.pinyin: Tā shì hěn duō háizi xīnzhōng de yīngxióng.
example.english: He is a hero in the hearts of many children.
example.fact: 雄's own component note explains that it originally described the male of a bird species (隹, "short-tailed bird") before extending to "male" generally and then to "heroic, grand" — a faint gendered echo still sitting underneath the modern, gender-neutral word for "hero."

examples.hanzi: 消防员是真正的英雄。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán shì zhēnzhèng de yīngxióng.
examples.english: Firefighters are real heroes.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的英雄是一位老师。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de yīngxióng shì yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.english: The hero of this movie is a teacher.

components.note: 土 (earth) — two people 从 sitting on the ground 土: to sit. Also in 座 zuò seat.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 请大家坐下。
example.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā zuòxia.
example.english: Everyone, please sit down.
example.fact: 下 attached after a verb like 坐 acts as a directional complement marking downward motion completed (坐下 "sit down," 躺下 "lie down," 蹲下 "squat down") — a small, reusable verb-plus-direction pattern that turns a bare verb into a specific physical action with a clear endpoint.

examples.hanzi: 你坐下吧，别站着。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuòxia ba, bié zhàn zhe.
examples.english: Sit down, don't stand.

examples.hanzi: 他一坐下就睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí zuòxia jiù shuìzháo le.
examples.english: He fell asleep as soon as he sat down.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 请说说你对这本书的感受。
example.pinyin: Qǐng shuōshuo nǐ duì zhè běn shū de gǎnshòu.
example.english: Please talk about your feelings about this book.
example.fact: 感受 names an inner, subjective impression formed through experience, while its near-synonym 感觉 leans more toward an immediate physical or intuitive sense ("it feels cold") — the two overlap heavily in casual speech, but 感受 skews slightly more reflective.

examples.hanzi: 我对这个城市的感受很特别。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè ge chéngshì de gǎnshòu hěn tèbié.
examples.english: My feelings about this city are very special.

examples.hanzi: 我感受到了大家的关心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnshòudàole dàjiā de guānxīn.
examples.english: I felt everyone's concern.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 这次事件引起了很多人的关注。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shìjiàn yǐnqǐle hěn duō rén de guānzhù.
example.english: This incident drew a lot of people's attention.
example.fact: 事件 leans toward a notable, often newsworthy occurrence — a scandal, accident, or historic happening — while the more general noun 事情 ("affair, matter") covers any ordinary task; calling a minor errand a 事件 would sound oddly dramatic.

examples.hanzi: 这是一次很特别的事件。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí cì hěn tèbié de shìjiàn.
examples.english: This is a very special incident.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在调查这起事件。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ shìjiàn.
examples.english: The police are investigating this incident.

meanings: measure word for sets and pairs

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting something in two, hence a second or secondary one.
畐 (fú) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 富 fù, 福 fú and 幅 fú.

example.hanzi: 他是我们公司的副经理。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de fù jīnglǐ.
example.english: He is the deputy manager of our company.
example.fact: 副 as a prefix means "deputy" or "vice": 副总统, 副校长, 副经理. As a measure word it counts matching sets: 一副眼镜 (a pair of glasses), 一副手套 (a pair of gloves), 一副扑克 (a deck of cards). 副作用 is a side effect.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个很好的副手。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de fùshǒu.
examples.english: He is a very good assistant.

examples.hanzi: 她给我买了一副新眼镜。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ mǎi le yí fù xīn yǎnjìng.
examples.english: She bought me a new pair of glasses.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and lips, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 吻 is a kiss.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for wěn; 物 wù shares the part.

example.hanzi: 他轻轻地吻了她。
example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de wěn le tā.
example.english: He gently kissed her.
example.fact: 吻 is the romantic or literary "kiss", used as both verb and noun (一个吻). In everyday speech people say 亲 (qīn) instead: 亲一下. 吻合 is an unrelated figurative use meaning "to match".

examples.hanzi: 妈妈吻了一下孩子的脸。
examples.pinyin: Māma wěn le yíxià háizi de liǎn.
examples.english: Mom kissed the child on the cheek.

examples.hanzi: 他们在机场吻别。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài jīchǎng wěnbié.
examples.english: They kissed goodbye at the airport.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 他犯了很大的罪。
example.pinyin: Tā fàn le hěn dà de zuì.
example.english: He committed a serious crime.
example.fact: 罪 is a crime or sin, as in 犯罪 (commit a crime) and 罪犯 (criminal). A colloquial twist is 受罪 ("endure guilt"): it means to suffer or go through hardship, as in 这天气真受罪, "this weather is torture".

examples.hanzi: 他认罪了，愿意接受惩罚。
examples.pinyin: Tā rènzuì le, yuànyì jiēshòu chéngfá.
examples.english: He pleaded guilty and is willing to accept punishment.

examples.hanzi: 别人犯的错，你不用受罪。
examples.pinyin: Biéren fàn de cuò, nǐ búyòng shòuzuì.
examples.english: You shouldn't have to suffer for other people's mistakes.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.

example.hanzi: 小偷从窗户逃走了。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu cóng chuānghu táozǒu le.
example.english: The thief escaped through the window.
example.fact: 逃 is to flee, often with a direction complement: 逃走, 逃跑. It also covers evading obligations, as in 逃课 (skip class) and 逃避 (avoid facing something, such as 逃避责任).

examples.hanzi: 他想逃，但是门锁着。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng táo, dànshì mén suǒ zhe.
examples.english: He wanted to flee, but the door was locked.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们逃课去玩游戏了。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen táo kè qù wán yóuxì le.
examples.english: The kids skipped class to play games.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 学校已经通知了所有家长。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǐjīng tōngzhīle suǒyǒu jiāzhǎng.
example.english: The school has already notified all the parents.
example.fact: 通知 works as both a verb ("to notify") and a noun ("a notice, notification") without changing form — like 工作 in the pilot batch, it's one more common case of a Chinese word doing double grammatical duty for free where English often needs two different words.

examples.hanzi: 会议时间有变化，请通知大家。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì shíjiān yǒu biànhuà, qǐng tōngzhī dàjiā.
examples.english: The meeting time has changed, please notify everyone.

examples.hanzi: 我收到了学校的通知。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōudàole xuéxiào de tōngzhī.
examples.english: I received a notice from the school.

meanings: have no choice or option but to

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 因为下雨,我们不得不取消野餐。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, wǒmen bùdébù qǔxiāo yěcān.
example.english: Because it rained, we had no choice but to cancel the picnic.
example.fact: 不得不 is built from a double-negative logic — 不 (not) + 得 (able to) + 不 (not) — literally "not able to not [do it]," the same double-negative-makes-a-forced-positive structure behind English "can't help but" or "cannot not."

examples.hanzi: 我不得不早点起床。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bùdébù zǎodiǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.english: I have to get up earlier.

examples.hanzi: 他病了，不得不住院。
examples.pinyin: Tā bìng le, bùdébù zhùyuàn.
examples.english: He's ill and has no choice but to be hospitalized.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 无论发生什么,我都会支持你。
example.pinyin: Wúlùn fāshēng shénme, wǒ dōu huì zhīchí nǐ.
example.english: No matter what happens, I will support you.
example.fact: 无论 sets up a clause that almost always closes with 都 later on ("无论...,都...") to mean "regardless of X, the outcome is always Y" — like 所有...都... in the pilot batch, it's the trailing 都 that actually carries the "no exceptions" meaning, while 无论 just introduces the range of possibilities.

examples.hanzi: 无论你去哪儿，我都跟着你。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn nǐ qù nǎr, wǒ dōu gēnzhe nǐ.
examples.english: No matter where you go, I'll follow you.

examples.hanzi: 无论天气怎么样，他都去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, tā dōu qù pǎobù.
examples.english: Whatever the weather, he goes running.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 妈妈慢慢放开了孩子的手。
example.pinyin: Māma mànmàn fàngkāile háizi de shǒu.
example.english: The mother slowly let go of the child's hand.
example.fact: 放开 pairs the verb 放 ("to release, put down") with the resultative complement 开 ("apart, open") to spell out the outcome of releasing — grip loosens until the two things are apart — the same verb-plus-开 pattern shows up in 打开 ("to open") and 拉开 ("to pull apart"), a productive way Chinese verbs specify their result.

examples.hanzi: 请放开我的手！
examples.pinyin: Qǐng fàngkāi wǒ de shǒu!
examples.english: Please let go of my hand!

examples.hanzi: 你要放开心胸，别想太多。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào fàngkāi xīnxiōng, bié xiǎng tài duō.
examples.english: You should open up your mind and not overthink.

components.note: 刀 — the picture of a knife blade; as 刂 on the right it marks cutting, as in 别, 利, 剪.

example.hanzi: 这把刀很锋利。
example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo hěn fēnglì.
example.english: This knife is very sharp.
example.fact: 刀 counts with 把 (一把刀). It forms 菜刀 (kitchen knife), 刀子 (knife) and 刀工 (knife skills in cooking). As the radical 刂 on the right of characters it signals cutting, as in 别 and 划.

examples.hanzi: 请用刀切一下面包。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng dāo qiē yíxià miànbāo.
examples.english: Please cut the bread with a knife.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一把新菜刀。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì bǎ xīn càidāo.
examples.english: I want to buy a new kitchen knife.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 后来,他搬到了北京。
example.pinyin: Hòulái, tā bāndàole Běijīng.
example.english: Afterwards, he moved to Beijing.
example.fact: 后来 can only point to a moment after some past reference point already established in the story or conversation — it cannot be used for the future the way English "later" sometimes can ("see you later" is never 后来见), which instead needs 以后 or 再见.

examples.hanzi: 后来我们成了好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Hòulái wǒmen chéngle hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: Later we became good friends.

examples.hanzi: 他一开始不喜欢，后来慢慢习惯了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì kāishǐ bù xǐhuan, hòulái mànmàn xíguàn le.
examples.english: He didn't like it at first, but gradually got used to it later.

components.note: 心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.hanzi: 我愿意帮你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yuànyì bāng nǐ.
example.english: I'm willing to help you.
example.fact: 愿 appears mostly in 愿意 (be willing), which is about consent or willingness rather than just wanting (想). It also forms 愿望 (wish) and 心愿 (heartfelt wish), and works in blessings: 愿你平安 ("may you be safe").

examples.hanzi: 我不愿意去，太远了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú yuànyì qù, tài yuǎn le.
examples.english: I don't want to go; it's too far.

examples.hanzi: 愿你每天都开心。
examples.pinyin: Yuàn nǐ měitiān dōu kāixīn.
examples.english: May you be happy every day.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 适 is to go to what suits you. 舌 is a simplification stand-in, not a real clue.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 这份工作很适合你。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò hěn shìhé nǐ.
example.english: This job suits you very well.
example.fact: 适合 takes its object directly, with no preposition needed (这份工作适合你, literally "this job suits you") — English speakers learning Chinese sometimes mistakenly insert 对 or 给 before the object by analogy with "suit to/for someone," but 适合 already functions as a complete transitive verb on its own.

examples.hanzi: 这件外套很适合你。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wàitào hěn shìhé nǐ.
examples.english: This coat suits you very well.

examples.hanzi: 这本书适合小孩子看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shìhé xiǎo háizi kàn.
examples.english: This book is suitable for children.

components.note: 厶 (bent arm/private) — the top part. How it joins 儿 to mean 'permit' is unclear. Memory aid: a person (儿) with a hand raised to say yes.
儿 (legs/person) — the bottom part and radical, as in 兄 and 先. It shows a person, but does not explain 允 on its own.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.

example.hanzi: 这里不允许吸烟。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù yǔnxǔ xīyān.
example.english: Smoking is not allowed here.
example.fact: 允许 is the more formal, written-register cousin of the everyday verb 让 ("to let, allow") — official rules, signs, and contracts reach for 允许 (不允许吸烟, "smoking not permitted"), while spoken Chinese much more often just says 不让 or 不能.

examples.hanzi: 老师不允许我们带手机。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bù yǔnxǔ wǒmen dài shǒujī.
examples.english: The teacher doesn't allow us to bring phones.

examples.hanzi: 如果时间允许，我想去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ shíjiān yǔnxǔ, wǒ xiǎng qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: If time permits, I'd like to travel.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,我很失望。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ hěn shīwàng.
example.english: Hearing this news, I was very disappointed.
example.fact: 失望 literally means "to lose hope" (失 "to lose" + 望 "to gaze, hope, expect") — 望 is traditionally pictured as a person standing on tiptoe, gazing up at the moon, an image of looking hopefully into the distance that 失望 turns into its opposite: hope lost.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试的结果让我很失望。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì de jiéguǒ ràng wǒ hěn shīwàng.
examples.english: The result of this exam disappointed me a lot.

examples.hanzi: 别让爸爸失望。
examples.pinyin: Bié ràng bàba shīwàng.
examples.english: Don't let Dad down.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 大家对这个计划有什么意见?
example.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège jìhuà yǒu shénme yìjiàn?
example.english: Does everyone have any opinions about this plan?
example.fact: 意见 covers both a neutral "opinion, viewpoint" and, in the fixed phrase 有意见 ("to have an objection, a complaint"), a sharper sense of disagreement or grievance — context alone decides which register is meant, since the same two characters serve both a mild and a critical reading.

examples.hanzi: 我对这件事没有意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè jiàn shì méiyǒu yìjiàn.
examples.english: I have no objection to this matter.

examples.hanzi: 你可以给我们提一些意见。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ gěi wǒmen tí yìxiē yìjiàn.
examples.english: You can give us some suggestions.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 她在比赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdéle dì yī míng.
example.english: She won first place in the competition.
example.fact: 获得 sits at the more formal, written end of the "get, obtain" spectrum — used for winning awards or gaining abstract things like 支持 ("support") or 信任 ("trust") — while the everyday verb 得到 covers much the same ground in ordinary conversation.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中获得了金牌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdéle jīnpái.
examples.english: He won a gold medal in the competition.

examples.hanzi: 多读书可以获得很多知识。
examples.pinyin: Duō dúshū kěyǐ huòdé hěn duō zhīshi.
examples.english: Reading more can help you gain a lot of knowledge.

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 要是明天不下雨,我们就去爬山。
example.pinyin: Yàoshi míngtiān bú xiàyǔ, wǒmen jiù qù páshān.
example.english: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we'll go hiking.
example.fact: 要是 is the casual, spoken-register twin of 如果 (also in the pilot batch) — both introduce a conditional clause and both commonly pair with a following 就, but 要是 sounds distinctly more colloquial and shows up far more in relaxed conversation than in formal writing.

examples.hanzi: 要是你有时间，就来我家玩。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi nǐ yǒu shíjiān, jiù lái wǒ jiā wán.
examples.english: If you have time, come to my place.

examples.hanzi: 要是我是你，我就不去。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ jiù bú qù.
examples.english: If I were you, I wouldn't go.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.hanzi: 我家离学校很近。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
example.english: My home is close to the school.
example.fact: 近 is the opposite of 远, with the key pattern A 离 B 很近 ("A is close to B"). 最近 means recently and 附近 means nearby. It also describes closeness of relationships, as in 亲近 (be close to).

examples.hanzi: 我们家离地铁站很近。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā lí dìtiězhàn hěn jìn.
examples.english: Our home is very close to the subway station.

examples.hanzi: 他最近很忙。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn hěn máng.
examples.english: He has been very busy recently.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 来参加的人数很多。
example.pinyin: Lái cānjiā de rénshù hěn duō.
example.english: The number of people who came is large.
example.fact: 数 has two common readings: shù means a number or amount (数字, 数学, 人数), and shǔ means to count (数一数, 数不清). The same character also appears in 数据 (data) and 数量 (quantity).

examples.hanzi: 这个月的学生人数比上个月多。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de xuésheng rénshù bǐ shàng gè yuè duō.
examples.english: The number of students this month is higher than last month.

examples.hanzi: 我数了一下，一共有十二个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ le yíxià, yígòng yǒu shí'èr gè rén.
examples.english: I counted, and there are twelve people in total.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室, 字; 寓 is a place of residence.
禺 (yù) sounds the same; also 遇 yù and 愚 yú.

example.hanzi: 他们住在一间小公寓里。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zhù zài yì jiān xiǎo gōngyù lǐ.
example.english: They live in a small apartment.
example.fact: 公寓 literally pairs 公 ("public, shared") with 寓 ("a residence, a dwelling") — together painting a home that is not a private, standalone house but one unit within a larger, shared building, the core idea behind "apartment" in any language.

examples.hanzi: 这座公寓楼有二十层。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gōngyù lóu yǒu èrshí céng.
examples.english: This apartment building has twenty floors.

examples.hanzi: 我打算租一间公寓。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn zū yì jiān gōngyù.
examples.english: I plan to rent an apartment.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 请把这份文件发给我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn wénjiàn fā gěi wǒ.
example.english: Please send this document to me.
example.fact: 文件 extended naturally from paper documents into computing, where it is now also the standard word for a digital "file" — the same semantic shift English "file" itself went through, from a physical folder of papers to a unit of digital data.

examples.hanzi: 我把文件存在电脑里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ wénjiàn cún zài diànnǎo lǐ le.
examples.english: I saved the file on my computer.

examples.hanzi: 这些文件需要经理签字。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē wénjiàn xūyào jīnglǐ qiānzì.
examples.english: These documents need the manager's signature.

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.hanzi: 因为票卖完了,我们只能站着看。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi piào màiwán le, wǒmen zhǐnéng zhànzhe kàn.
example.english: Since the tickets sold out, we could only watch standing up.
example.fact: 只能 marks a constrained, no-better-option ability — "can only, forced to" — distinct from 能 alone, which stays neutral about whether other options exist; adding 只 turns a plain statement of capability into an implicit complaint about limited choices.

examples.hanzi: 我只能明天再来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ néng míngtiān zài lái.
examples.english: I can only come again tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 没有车，我们只能走路回去。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu chē, wǒmen zhǐ néng zǒulù huíqù.
examples.english: With no car, we can only walk back.

components.note: 寸 (inch, hand) — measuring and hands: 对, 导, 寺; 寻 traditionally meant stretching arms to measure, then searching.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 找 is to search with the hands. The right part 戈 is not a useful clue.

example.hanzi: 他一直在寻找失踪的猫。
example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài xúnzhǎo shīzōng de māo.
example.english: He has been searching for his missing cat all along.
example.fact: 寻找 is a more formal, written-feeling synonym for the everyday verb 找 alone ("to look for") — it doubles up two verbs that each independently mean "to search" (寻 and 找), the same reinforcing word-building strategy seen in 喜欢 and 舞蹈, elevating the register slightly above bare 找.

examples.hanzi: 我正在寻找新的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài xúnzhǎo xīn de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I am looking for a new job.

examples.hanzi: 人们一直在寻找幸福。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen yìzhí zài xúnzhǎo xìngfú.
examples.english: People are always seeking happiness.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一件白衬衫。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
example.english: She is wearing a white shirt.
example.fact: 白 also means "in vain" (白跑一趟, a wasted trip) and "for free" (白吃白喝, to freeload). It builds 白天 (daytime) and 明白 (to understand), and white is the colour of mourning in traditional Chinese culture.

examples.hanzi: 今天天气很好，天上有白云。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo, tiānshang yǒu bái yún.
examples.english: The weather is nice today, with white clouds in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 我白跑了一趟，他不在家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bái pǎole yí tàng, tā bú zàijiā.
examples.english: I made the trip for nothing; he wasn't home.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions of striking or acting: 教, 放, 改, 政; 攻 is to attack.
工 (gōng) sounds exactly like 攻; also in 功 gōng, 红 hóng, 空 kōng.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 敌军突然发起了攻击。
example.pinyin: Dí jūn tūrán fāqǐle gōngjī.
example.english: The enemy army suddenly launched an attack.
example.fact: 攻击 covers both literal, physical attacks (military or otherwise) and abstract verbal ones (人身攻击, "a personal attack, an ad hominem") — much like English "attack" itself stretches from a punch to a cutting remark, Chinese did not need a separate word for the metaphorical extension either.

examples.hanzi: 他的话攻击了很多人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà gōngjīle hěn duō rén.
examples.english: His words attacked many people.

examples.hanzi: 网络上有人攻击这位歌手。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò shàng yǒu rén gōngjī zhè wèi gēshǒu.
examples.english: Someone online is attacking this singer.
